whitelist.reason: B3. The configurator modal, deleted from every page that cannot open it. This is the change WP-0b-i wrote, measured and REVERTED rather than ship (see _notes.wp0bi_fix): the include was sitewide, so 16 built pages carried id="saunaModal" and exactly one of them -- /saunas/, the only page with data-action="open-modal" -- could use it, leaving 15 routes shipping a second inert <form> beside their real contact form. It could not be certified then because delete-subtree capped its slice search at MAX_SUBTREE_TOKENS = 64 and this subtree is 355 tokens, and raising a cap to make its own batch go green is the move this instrument exists to refuse. It ships here as its own batch carrying the cap raise (64 -> 400) as a separately reviewed subject, with Z18-Z20 and D-m16 certifying the raised cap independently of this entry. SPAN AND HASH RE-MEASURED against this comparison's own baseline build, not carried forward: WP-0b-i recorded span 352 / hash c3a120b59594b6b1 and BOTH have moved (355 / e379071f602ee944) because the modal markup changed between then and now. The old hash is dead and is not what this entry declares. Measured uniformly -- every route, both widths, identical hash and span -- so the modal is not width- or page-dependent. COUNT is 1 per page/width comparison, and it consumes on 32 of them. _notes.authority: This whitelist is a DECLARATION, not a mute button. Every entry names a change, a count, a reason and the commit that made it legitimate. An undeclared change fails; a declared change that does not occur ALSO fails, because a stale entry is a hole nobody closed. Counts are per page/width comparison.
_notes.widths: Each page is loaded at both widths and fingerprinted separately. The site is responsive by CSS, so both widths should yield IDENTICAL markup -- if a page's DOM turns out to be width-dependent it is reported as a width anomaly, because a DOM-integrity result for such a page is per-width rather than general.
_notes.volatile: Two URL segments are normalized before comparison and nothing else: the ?v= content-hash cache stamp (P-A -- it changes whenever styles.css or a js/ file changes, which is exactly what a restyle does) and the hash segment of /fonts/<name>.<hash>.woff2 (the family name is KEPT, so substituting a different typeface still fails). Whether the bytes behind a font name are the right typeface is the fonts suite's question; it asserts computed faces against a real browser. Every other attribute compares raw.
_notes.text: Text is whitespace-normalized (rendering collapses whitespace anyway) and otherwise compared EXACTLY. A reworded sentence, a changed price or a dropped word is a failure. That is the instrument's purpose, not a limitation of it.
_notes.specificity: Every entry's "contains" must identify the node, not a family of nodes: the run refuses to start if an entry matches more nodes in the relevant build than it declares. A count is a budget, not an identity -- an entry held in check by its count alone consumes the first n matching changes rather than the ones it was written for, and starts absorbing a different node the moment the intended one stops changing. This is why the two Google preconnects are two entries keyed on their exact hrefs rather than one entry matching the word "preconnect" (which also matches the Cloudinary hint that must survive), and why the font preloads key on as="font" rather than "preload" (which also matches the hero image preload).
_notes.wp1b: WP-1b's full certification map, range-scoped to 198c0bb..c208508 (the batch commits vs their parent). Six reveal-class renames, six further class renames, six class REMOVALS (to:null -- the rhythm utilities and the cut warm-glow), two delete-subtree entries for the hero-intro hold, an added/removed pair for the five inline image radii, and a kind:code pair for booking-ops.html's reconciled --color-bg. Every count is measured against the real builds, not budgeted: the earlier note here recorded that the residual was wider than the four declared change classes and refused to widen the map to go green. This map is that residual ENUMERATED, which is the opposite move -- each line names one change, its reason and its commit, and the run reports what each consumed.
_notes.staleness: These four entries are the WP-1a declaration (commit 1877955 vs its parent) and they are the FIXTURE DATA for scripts/dom-integrity.test.mjs -- A1, A3, W8 and two mutation-battery properties (D-m6, D-m7) lose their coverage entirely without them. WP-1b tried removing them as stale and the suite caught it, which is the fixture-wins rule working. Consequence, stated so nobody rediscovers it as a bug: run this instrument against any baseline at or after 1877955 and all four report STALE WHITELIST, because the changes they declare are present on BOTH sides of that comparison. The entries are not wrong and the staleness check is not wrong -- the whitelist is per-COMPARISON while the file is per-repo, and the `commit` field records which comparison an entry belongs to without anything reading it. Resolving that is a harness change, not a batch change; flagged, not attempted here.
_notes.scope: Every entry declares the comparison it belongs to as "range": "<baselineSha>..<candidateSha>". The file is per-repo but each entry describes ONE batch's change, so without a scope an old batch's declarations sit here forever, reading stale against every later baseline while still being load-bearing. Out-of-scope entries are INERT for a run -- reported so they can be pruned, never consuming a diff they were not written for.
_notes.renameMap: An "op": "rename" entry declares an old->new CLASS TOKEN pair, applied to the BASELINE's vocabulary before anything is compared. Whole tokens only, never substrings, so renaming `fade-in` cannot touch `fade-in-late`. Everything the map does not explain survives into the comparison and still fails: a rename plus a smuggled extra class fails naming the smuggled token. A rename whose `from` never appears is flagged stale, so dead declarations cannot accumulate. A "to" of null declares that the token was REMOVED rather than renamed: the element survives and one of its class tokens goes, which no node entry can express. Same strictness -- an undeclared removal on the same node still fails.
_notes.deleteSubtree: A "delete-subtree" entry names a deleted node by tag + ancestry path + a HASH of its own serialized content, and consumes the whole run of removed tokens or nothing. It exists for attribute-less nodes, where the only substrings a `contains` entry could use are exactly the lazy kind the specificity check rejects. The hash cannot be written from memory -- it is measured from the baseline build -- and an entry whose hash matches nothing there is reported before any verdict rests on it. A nested subtree is ONE entry, not one per element.
_notes.kind: A removed/added entry names an ELEMENT unless it declares kind:"code" or kind:"text", in which case `contains` is matched against the token's TEXT. Without it an edit to an inline <style> body is undeclarable by construction, which is how booking-ops.html's :root reconciliation had no way to be certified. Kind is part of the entry's identity: a code entry cannot consume an element change even when its substring appears in an attribute.
_notes.wp0bi_fix: WP-0b-i's fix round, range-scoped to 83421b9..dec32ac. Two change classes: aria-expanded and aria-controls on the mobile menu toggle, and aria-hidden on 21 decorative comparison glyphs on /saunas/. NOT DONE, and recorded here rather than quietly dropped: scoping the configurator modal to /saunas/, the only page with anything that opens it. Sitewide it puts a second inert <form> on 15 routes whose empty `configuration`, `model` and `estimated_total` hidden inputs sit in the DOM beside the real contact form (route count MEASURED and corrected 2026-08-01, was recorded as 18 from memory: `grep -rl 'id="saunaModal"' dist/` after a clean build returns 16 built pages carrying the modal, of 19 HTML pages total, and `grep -rl 'open-modal' dist/` returns exactly one of them -- /saunas/ -- so 15 carry the modal and cannot open it) -- a behavioural reviewer read the /contact/ one as a live field that had lost its data. The change is right and it was written and measured (one deleted subtree, span 352, hash c3a120b59594b6b1). It cannot be CERTIFIED today: delete-subtree caps its slice search at MAX_SUBTREE_TOKENS = 64, stated in the harness as a real limit whose safe direction is to fail loudly. Raising the cap to make this batch's own change pass is the tuning-until-green move this instrument exists to refuse, and a harness change does not belong in a fix round. Reverted, and handed on as its own small batch that carries the harness change with it. The honeypot's inline padding was left alone for a related reason: it is offscreen and untappable, its 34x34 measurement is an artefact of the global input rule, and its markup is identical to the copy inside the modal, so any declaration naming one would consume the other. The JS RUN FAILURE is expected here and waived nowhere: this instrument certifies delivered markup with scripts disabled, and the batch changes modal.js and navigation.js by design. What the scripts do is certified by scripts/quote-funnel.test.mjs, which drives them in a real browser through every state including the two defects this round fixed. Read the two together. _notes.b1JsRunFailure: Wave B-1 batch B1 (hero-first reveal) reports a JS RUN FAILURE against fc65d61, and it is expected rather than waived. This instrument certifies DELIVERED MARKUP with scripts disabled and refuses to vouch for a comparison whose client JavaScript changed; B1 necessarily edits js/animations.js (SETTLE_MS retarget, the load-in ordering, the escape hatch), so the run failure is structural to the batch and cannot be designed away -- the same shape as the precedent recorded at the :650 narrative. The markup half IS certified: the six declarations above consumed 1 each per page/width across both widths and no undeclared change remains. The behavioural half is certified by the events suite, which drives the real built site in a real browser -- 49 passing, including the agreement fixture (computed transition delay + duration === SETTLE_MS), the LCP invariant (the hero is never a reveal target), the Tab-during-the-beat fixture, and the untouched anti-lock invariants. Read the two together; do not read a dom-integrity PASS as covering the script.
_notes.b1Range: How to reproduce Wave B-1 batch B1's markup certificate, and why its range ends where it does. The six B1 entries are range-scoped fc65d61..c3ed9cd, and entries apply only when the RUN's candidate sha matches the range end -- so the certifying invocation is `node scripts/dom-integrity.mjs --baseline fc65d61 --candidate c3ed9cd`, with the config read from the working tree. c3ed9cd is the last B1 commit that changes delivered markup; the commits after it touch only scripts/, configs and ROADMAP.md, none of which reach a template or a hashed asset, so they produce byte-identical dist HTML. (Within the batch as a whole that is NOT true of the eighteen non-home pages: styles.css and js/ changed, so their ?v= cache-bust stamps moved. The dom-integrity instrument normalizes that stamp -- see _notes.volatile -- which is why those pages still compare identical.) Running with the default candidate WORKING reports the six as undeclared, which is the range mechanism behaving correctly, not a regression -- a declaration that stayed live past the commits it describes is the 'load-bearing forever' failure the scope rule at _notes.scope exists to prevent. The next batch baselines on B1's tip, where these entries correctly go inert.
